newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 2.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
** The government on Wednesday issued an order on Wednesday allowing investment in shares issued by public companies to be exempt from long-term capital gains tax.
** The newly appointed chairman of the Unit Trust of India, (UTI) the country's biggest mutual fund says he is bullish on the stock markets.
"The bad phase of the capital market is over. We are now
in a bullish phase. The brighter days are here again, and UTI is bullish that the (Bombay) Sensex will touch the 4,000 mark by March, 1997," UTI chairman Gyan Praksh Gupta told the Financial Express.
** Indian merchandise exports fell 3.8 percent to $2.48 billion in November from $2.58 billion in the same month in 1995.
** The finance ministry said the easing of a gold import restriction announced earlier this week would be effective from New Year's Day.
"The enhancement limit of 10 kg (22 lbs) up to which
gold can be imported by passengers would come into force from 1st January, 1998," a finance ministry statement said.
** The Reserve Bank of India said foreign currency assets rose by $2.29 billion to $19.76 billion in calendar year 1996.
** Indian shares began the new year on a bullish note with blue chips rallying on a flurry of local buying after the government said it would announce a plan to boost the country's capital markets.
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) 30-share index surged 175.36 points, or 5.7 percent, to 3,260.56.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index rose 40.45 points, or 4.5 percent, to 939.55.
The Delhi index gained 22.72 points, or 3.3 percent, to 712.25.
